GBS pipeline walkthrough

A graph followed through every step of the GBS finder: the adjacency matrix, the squeezing and interferometer derived from it, the photonic circuit, the photons the simulator returns, and how each photon pattern becomes a candidate subgraph and then a cluster. Pick a graph, the mean photon number n, the finder and the sampler above; n sets both the squeezing of the circuit and the edge threshold. The simulators cannot run in the browser, so every n from 1 to 10 was run in advance.

Sampling setup: n is the mean photon number in total across all modes; the Piquasso sampler draws a new seed for every call (randomize_piquasso_seed=True), so every batch has new shots; and the gate-based readout puts classical bit c[0] first. See docs/gbs_sampling_bugs.md for why each of these matters.

1–10, precomputed

1The graph

2Adjacency matrix

3From matrix to circuit parameters

GBS encodes the graph in a Gaussian state. Piquasso's decompose_adjacency_matrix_into_circuit takes the Takagi decomposition of the scaled matrix, giving one squeezing value per mode and an interferometer:

c·A = U · diag(tanh r₀, tanh r₁, …) · Uᵀ, ⟨n⟩ = Σᵢ sinh²(rᵢ)

The scale c is chosen so the mean photon number ⟨n⟩ hits a target. The probability of a photon pattern on a set of nodes S grows with |Haf(A_S)|², the squared number of perfect matchings of the subgraph on S, which is why dense subgraphs come out more often.

Squeezing r per mode

Interferometer |U|

4The photonic circuit

commons.generate_circuit turns the parameters into a Blackbird program: one squeezer per mode, then the interferometer split by the Clements decomposition into a mesh of beam splitters on neighbouring modes and phase shifters. Mode i carries graph node i. Hover a gate for its parameters.

5Sampled photons

The simulator measures the photon number in every mode, 10 shots per batch. Only binary shots, with at most one photon per mode, can be read as a set of nodes; the others are dropped.

6From photons to subgraphs

Each binary shot with at least two photons names a set of nodes. _find_densest_subgraph skips repeated node sets and disconnected subgraphs, and keeps the one with the most edges. A batch is accepted when that count reaches the threshold n(n−1)/2 − k

7From subgraphs to clusters

The kept subgraph becomes a cluster and its nodes are removed. The next round builds a new circuit on the smaller graph and samples again, until the remaining graph has no edges. The segmentation engine keeps only the first cluster (--gbs-max-clusters-per-graph 1); later rounds are shown to make the loop visible.
